{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018PbQphDCTU6TbtK2MEcyKE","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Strateq Health, Inc. — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-16\n     4→Developer website: https://www.strateqhealth.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Strateq Health, Inc. is a healthcare IT company focused on providing a cloud-based Hospital Information System (HIS) / EHR to critical access hospitals, rural and small community hospitals, and freestanding emergency rooms. The company is a subsidiary or division of Strateq Group, a Malaysia-based technology conglomerate that has been \"redefining industries since 1983.\" Strateq Group operates across offices in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Hong Kong, China, and the USA. Their healthcare division claims 22+ years of experience building and operating hospital information systems across 30+ hospitals internationally (primarily Malaysia, with expansion into the US market).\n     9→\n    10→The US entity, Strateq Health, Inc., is headquartered in Plano, Texas (previously referenced as Houston in some materials). Co-founders are Datuk Tan Seng Kit (CEO) and CheeSiong Yee (COO & CTO). A 2019 press release via GlobeNewsWire cited 600+ employees globally, though the US team appears much smaller — the about page lists roughly six named leadership positions. The Strateq Group parent site references a product called \"37 Degrees\" as their cloud HIS offering, which appears to be the same underlying platform marketed as \"StrateqEHR\" in the US market.\n    11→\n    12→The company's go-to-market targets the financially constrained rural/critical access hospital segment, emphasizing SaaS pricing (monthly fee, no upfront CapEx) and AWS cloud hosting secured by ARMOR. Named customers include ADHS and Nutex Health. Strateq exhibited at the 2019 TORCH (Texas Organization of Rural & Community Hospitals) conference, consistent with their rural hospital focus.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: StrateqEHR\n    15→\n    16→CHPL ID: 10778 (15.05.05.3097.STRQ.01.00.1.220105)\n    17→Version: 5\n    18→Certified: 2022-01-05\n    19→SED Intended Users: Inpatient physicians and nurses\n    20→\n    21→### What It Is\n    22→\n    23→StrateqEHR is described as \"the first fully integrated, native cloud-based HIS\" — a comprehensive hospital information system, not just an EHR module. It is designed to serve as a single platform covering clinical, financial/revenue cycle, and ancillary/departmental functions for small hospitals and freestanding ERs. The product is cloud-native on AWS, SaaS-delivered, and accessible from any web-enabled device.\n    24→\n    25→The certified product appears to be the full HIS platform — not a component of something larger. The certification criteria are broad (30+ criteria spanning clinical data, care transitions, CQMs, public health reporting, APIs, and patient data access), consistent with a comprehensive inpatient system.\n    26→\n    27→### Users & Market\n    28→\n    29→**Primary users**: Inpatient physicians, nurses, HIM staff, registration/admitting staff, pharmacy, billing/revenue cycle staff, and hospital administrators.\n    30→\n    31→**Target settings**: Critical access hospitals, rural hospitals, small community hospitals, and freestanding emergency rooms. The system explicitly advertises configurations for both inpatient hospital and freestanding ER workflows.\n    32→\n    33→**Customer base**: The vendor claims 30+ hospital deployments internationally (across the Strateq Group parent). Named US references include ADHS and Nutex Health (a freestanding ER chain). Customer count in the US specifically is unclear — this appears to be a small-footprint vendor in the US market.\n    34→\n    35→**Reviews**: A Capterra listing exists but was inaccessible. A few reviews on Five.Reviews show mixed feedback — some praising customer service, others complaining about pricing and performance. No G2 or KLAS profiles were found, which is consistent with a small/niche vendor.\n    36→\n    37→### Modules & Functionality\n    38→\n    39→The vendor website organizes the product into four solution areas: Clinical Solutions, Revenue Cycle, Ancillary Solutions, and Freestanding ER. Here is what the vendor describes:\n    40→\n    41→**Patient Administration / ADT**\n    42→- Patient registration and quick registration (ER)\n    43→- Admission, discharge, transfer (ADT) workflows\n    44→- Bed management\n    45→- Insurance verification and pre-authorization\n    46→- Scheduling (including perioperative resource scheduling)\n    47→\n    48→**Clinical Documentation**\n    49→- Patent-pending \"Dynamic Form Engine\" that renders clinical forms (H&P, care plans, admission assessments, nursing shift assessments) on-the-fly based on definitions by clinical informatics\n    50→- Provider documentation and nursing documentation\n    51→- Nursing care plans\n    52→- Dictation notes\n    53→- CCDA record generation\n    54→\n    55→**CPOE (Computerized Provider Order Entry)**\n    56→- Close-loop CPOE for nursing orders, procedure orders, medication orders, laboratory orders, and radiology orders\n    57→- Complaint-specific order sets (particularly for ED workflows)\n    58→- Drug interaction and allergy checking\n    59→\n    60→**Pharmacy / Medication Management**\n    61→- Integrated pharmacy module\n    62→- First Databank (FDB) drug database integration\n    63→- SureScripts integration for e-prescribing\n    64→- Allergy and drug interaction checking\n    65→- Medication reconciliation\n    66→- Home medication plans, nursing notes, dictation notes, operative notes — rendered via their Dynamic Form Engine)\n   138→- **Orders** (medications, labs, radiology, nursing, procedures — via close-loop CPOE)\n   139→- **Medication data** (prescriptions, medication lists, home medications, medication reconciliation, eMAR administration records, allergy lists)\n   140→- **Lab results** (via Aspyra CyberLAB integration — unclear if StrateqEHR stores results directly or interfaces to a separate LIS)\n   141→- **Vital signs and clinical observations** (referenced in patient dashboard and ED tracking board)\n   142→- **ED tracking data** (location, ESI level, arrival times, disposition, length of stay)\n   143→- **Scanned documents and images** (via HIM document scanning module)\n   144→- **Medical record deficiency tracking data**\n   145→- **Billing and claims data** (charges, claims, remittance, eligibility, denials, GL journal entries, patient account balances)\n   146→- **Scheduling data** (patient appointments, perioperative resource scheduling)\n   147→- **CCDA documents** (transitions of care)\n   148→- **Immunization records** (for registry reporting)\n   149→- **Syndromic surveillance data**\n   150→- **Clinical quality measure data** (CQMs)\n   151→- **Audit logs** (required by (d)(1)–(d)(9) certification)\n   152→- **Patient portal data** (via Bridge — messages, payments; exact data stored in StrateqEHR vs. Bridge is unclear)\n   153→\n   154→**Gaps/Uncertainties**:\n   155→- **Laboratory**: The integration with Aspyra CyberLAB is listed as additional third-party software. It's unclear how deeply lab data is stored within StrateqEHR versus the external LIS. The close-loop CPOE handles lab ordering, and results presumably flow back, but the boundary is unclear.\n   156→- **Radiology/Imaging**: CPOE supports radiology orders, but no PACS or radiology module is described. Radiology likely involves an external system with order/result interfaces.\n   157→- **Patient portal content**: Bridge Patient Portal is a third-party product. What data is stored in Bridge vs. StrateqEHR (e.g., patient messages, portal activity logs) is unclear.\n   158→- **Implantable device data**: Certified for (a)(14) which requires tracking unique device identifiers (UDIs), so this data should be stored.\n   159→- **Specific ancillary department data**: The \"Ancillary Solutions\" area is mentioned as a category on the solutions page but no detail was found on what specific ancillary modules (dietary, respiratory therapy, etc.) are included.\n   160→\n   161→---\n   162→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. The company is a subsidiary or division of Strateq Group, a Malaysia-based technology conglomerate that has been \"redefining industries since 1983.\" Strateq Group operates across offices in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Hong Kong, China, and the USA. Their healthcare division claims 22+ years of experience building and operating hospital information systems across 30+ hospitals internationally (primarily Malaysia, with expansion into the US market).\n\nThe US entity, Strateq Health, Inc., is headquartered in Plano, Texas (previously referenced as Houston in some materials). Co-founders are Datuk Tan Seng Kit (CEO) and CheeSiong Yee (COO & CTO). A 2019 press release via GlobeNewsWire cited 600+ employees globally, though the US team appears much smaller — the about page lists roughly six named leadership positions. The Strateq Group parent site references a product called \"37 Degrees\" as their cloud HIS offering, which appears to be the same underlying platform marketed as \"StrateqEHR\" in the US market.\n\nThe company's go-to-market targets the financially constrained rural/critical access hospital segment, emphasizing SaaS pricing (monthly fee, no upfront CapEx) and AWS cloud hosting secured by ARMOR. Named customers include ADHS and Nutex Health. Strateq exhibited at the 2019 TORCH (Texas Organization of Rural & Community Hospitals) conference, consistent with their rural hospital focus.\n\n## Product: StrateqEHR\n\nCHPL ID: 10778 (15.05.05.3097.STRQ.01.00.1.220105)\nVersion: 5\nCertified: 2022-01-05\nSED Intended Users: Inpatient physicians and nurses\n\n### What It Is\n\nStrateqEHR is described as \"the first fully integrated, native cloud-based HIS\" — a comprehensive hospital information system, not just an EHR module. It is designed to serve as a single platform covering clinical, financial/revenue cycle, and ancillary/departmental functions for small hospitals and freestanding ERs. The product is cloud-native on AWS, SaaS-delivered, and accessible from any web-enabled device.\n\nThe certified product appears to be the full HIS platform — not a component of something larger. The certification criteria are broad (30+ criteria spanning clinical data, care transitions, CQMs, public health reporting, APIs, and patient data access), consistent with a comprehensive inpatient system.\n\n### Users & Market\n\n**Primary users**: Inpatient physicians, nurses, HIM staff, registration/admitting staff, pharmacy, billing/revenue cycle staff, and hospital administrators.\n\n**Target settings**: Critical access hospitals, rural hospitals, small community hospitals, and freestanding emergency rooms. The system explicitly advertises configurations for both inpatient hospital and freestanding ER workflows.\n\n**Customer base**: The vendor claims 30+ hospital deployments internationally (across the Strateq Group parent). Named US references include ADHS and Nutex Health (a freestanding ER chain). Customer count in the US specifically is unclear — this appears to be a small-footprint vendor in the US market.\n\n**Reviews**: A Capterra listing exists but was inaccessible. A few reviews on Five.Reviews show mixed feedback — some praising customer service, others complaining about pricing and performance. No G2 or KLAS profiles were found, which is consistent with a small/niche vendor.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nThe vendor website organizes the product into four solution areas: Clinical Solutions, Revenue Cycle, Ancillary Solutions, and Freestanding ER. Here is what the vendor describes:\n\n**Patient Administration / ADT**\n- Patient registration and quick registration (ER)\n- Admission, discharge, transfer (ADT) workflows\n- Bed management\n- Insurance verification and pre-authorization\n- Scheduling (including perioperative resource scheduling)\n\n**Clinical Documentation**\n- Patent-pending \"Dynamic Form Engine\" that renders clinical forms (H&P, care plans, admission assessments, nursing shift assessments) on-the-fly based on definitions by clinical informatics\n- Provider documentation and nursing documentation\n- Nursing care plans\n- Dictation notes\n- CCDA record generation\n\n**CPOE (Computerized Provider Order Entry)**\n- Close-loop CPOE for nursing orders, procedure orders, medication orders, laboratory orders, and radiology orders\n- Complaint-specific order sets (particularly for ED workflows)\n- Drug interaction and allergy checking\n\n**Pharmacy / Medication Management**\n- Integrated pharmacy module\n- First Databank (FDB) drug database integration\n- SureScripts integration for e-prescribing\n- Allergy and drug interaction checking\n- Medication reconciliation\n- Home medication management\n- eMAR (electronic medication administration record)\n\n**Emergency Department**\n- ED tracking board (updates patient location, arrival time, ESI level, vital signs, provider, length of stay, disposition, order status)\n- Triage documentation\n- ED-specific nursing documentation templates\n- ED daily log reporting\n- Process turnaround time reports\n- State and local reporting\n- Integrated discharge workflow with ePrescribing\n\n**Nursing**\n- Care plans\n- Assessments\n- eMAR\n- Patient and unit worklists\n- Nursing Kardex\n\n**Perioperative**\n- Patient and resource scheduling\n- Operative checklists\n- Clinical documentation\n- Order entry\n\n**HIM / Medical Records**\n- Patient master record management\n- Document scanning and management\n- Deficiency tracking\n- Release of information (ROI)\n\n**Revenue Cycle Management**\n- Integrated with Waystar for claims processing\n- Clinical data capture and charge capture at point of care\n- Real-time eligibility checking via Waystar (hundreds of payers)\n- 3M CRS coding integration with automatic claim generation\n- Electronic remittance processing and manual paper remit entry\n- Credit card and check authorization with real-time posting\n- Daily automated claim submission to Waystar\n- Denial management with pre-defined denial templates via Waystar\n- Patient statement generation (email and USPS via Waystar)\n- Patient portal for credit/debit card payments\n- Real-time GL journal entries\n- Reporting: patient accounts, claims, remittance, payer data\n\n**Patient Portal**\n- Via Bridge Patient Portal (third-party integration)\n- Supports patient payment (credit/debit)\n\n**Interoperability / Data Exchange**\n- CCDA generation and exchange for transitions of care\n- Clinical information reconciliation\n- e-Prescribing via SureScripts/NewCrop\n- FHIR API access (g)(7)–(g)(10) certified\n- Public health reporting: immunization registry and syndromic surveillance\n- Clinical Quality Measures (CQMs) including antithrombotic therapy and opioid safety measures\n\n**Third-party Integrations Referenced on Certification Page**\n- FDB (First Databank) — drug database\n- Aspyra CyberLAB — laboratory information system\n- Bridge Patient Portal — patient portal\n- NewCrop — e-prescribing\n- Waystar — revenue cycle / claims clearinghouse\n- 3M CRS — coding\n- ARMOR — cloud security\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the vendor's described modules and features, StrateqEHR stores and manages:\n\n- **Patient demographics and registration data** (including insurance information, pre-authorization data)\n- **Clinical documentation** (H&P, assessments, care plans, nursing notes, dictation notes, operative notes — rendered via their Dynamic Form Engine)\n- **Orders** (medications, labs, radiology, nursing, procedures — via close-loop CPOE)\n- **Medication data** (prescriptions, medication lists, home medications, medication reconciliation, eMAR administration records, allergy lists)\n- **Lab results** (via Aspyra CyberLAB integration — unclear if StrateqEHR stores results directly or interfaces to a separate LIS)\n- **Vital signs and clinical observations** (referenced in patient dashboard and ED tracking board)\n- **ED tracking data** (location, ESI level, arrival times, disposition, length of stay)\n- **Scanned documents and images** (via HIM document scanning module)\n- **Medical record deficiency tracking data**\n- **Billing and claims data** (charges, claims, remittance, eligibility, denials, GL journal entries, patient account balances)\n- **Scheduling data** (patient appointments, perioperative resource scheduling)\n- **CCDA documents** (transitions of care)\n- **Immunization records** (for registry reporting)\n- **Syndromic surveillance data**\n- **Clinical quality measure data** (CQMs)\n- **Audit logs** (required by (d)(1)–(d)(9) certification)\n- **Patient portal data** (via Bridge — messages, payments; exact data stored in StrateqEHR vs. Bridge is unclear)\n\n**Gaps/Uncertainties**:\n- **Laboratory**: The integration with Aspyra CyberLAB is listed as additional third-party software. It's unclear how deeply lab data is stored within StrateqEHR versus the external LIS. The close-loop CPOE handles lab ordering, and results presumably flow back, but the boundary is unclear.\n- **Radiology/Imaging**: CPOE supports radiology orders, but no PACS or radiology module is described. Radiology likely involves an external system with order/result interfaces.\n- **Patient portal content**: Bridge Patient Portal is a third-party product. What data is stored in Bridge vs. StrateqEHR (e.g., patient messages, portal activity logs) is unclear.\n- **Implantable device data**: Certified for (a)(14) which requires tracking unique device identifiers (UDIs), so this data should be stored.\n- **Specific ancillary department data**: The \"Ancillary Solutions\" area is mentioned as a category on the solutions page but no detail was found on what specific ancillary modules (dietary, respiratory therapy, etc.) are included.\n\n---\n","numLines":162,"startLine":1,"totalLines":162}}}

5\nINTRODUCTION\n\nIn this documentation we will list all the steps required to access protected health information based on the documentation of an open API. The\nAPI makes health information broadly available using FHIR®, a set of clinical interoperability resources under the umbrella of the HL7 standards\norganization. FHIR is based on common web standards can be reached through a RESTful protocol in which each FHIR resource has a known\nURL. This document describes OAuth 2.0 for client applications to authorize, authenticate, and integrate with FHIR-based data systems.\nWe follow Smart-On-FHIR authentication (OAuth2) and authorization. (Ref: https://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/STU2/)\n\nFHIR Endpoints\nNote: Production and Test Server endpoints are subject to change.\n\nProduction Endpoint\n•\n\nFHIR : https://testfhir.strateqhealth.com:9443/fhirserver/fhir/\n\n•\n\nAuthentication Server: https://testauth.strateqhealth.com/\n\nTest Server Endpoint\n•\n•\n\nFHIR : https://testfhir.strateqhealth.com:9443/fhirserver/fhir/\nAuthentication Server: https://testauth.strateqhealth.com/\n\nTypes of Smart-On-FHIR applications\n•\n\nStandalone App : SMART on FHIR confidential client with a patient context, refresh token, and OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity\ntoken.\n\n•\n\nEHR Embedded app: Demonstrate the ability to perform an EHR launch to a SMART on FHIR\n\n•\n\nSmart Backend Services App (Multi-patient authorization and API) : These are server-to-server backend applications e.g. Export\nclinical data for multiple patients in a group. This app is system level app without any UI.\n\nTypes of Authentications supported\n•\n\nSymmetric (“client secret”) authentication\n\n•\n\nAsymmetric (“private key JWT”) authentication\n\n•\n\nPublic 5\nINTRODUCTION\n\nIn this documentation we will list all the steps required to access protected health information based on the documentation of an open API. The\nAPI makes health information broadly available using FHIR®, a set of clinical interoperability resources under the umbrella of the HL7 standards\norganization. FHIR is based on common web standards can be reached through a RESTful protocol in which each FHIR resource has a known\nURL. This document describes OAuth 2.0 for client applications to authorize, authenticate, and integrate with FHIR-based data systems.\nWe follow Smart-On-FHIR authentication (OAuth2) and authorization. (Ref: https://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/STU2/)\n\nFHIR Endpoints\nNote: Production and Test Server endpoints are subject to change.\n\nProduction Endpoint\n•\n\nFHIR : https://testfhir.strateqhealth.com:9443/fhirserver/fhir/\n\n•\n\nAuthentication Server: https://testauth.strateqhealth.com/\n\nTest Server Endpoint\n•\n•\n\nFHIR : https://testfhir.strateqhealth.com:9443/fhirserver/fhir/\nAuthentication Server: https://testauth.strateqhealth.com/\n\nTypes of Smart-On-FHIR applications\n•\n\nStandalone App : SMART on FHIR confidential client with a patient context, refresh token, and OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity\ntoken.\n\n•\n\nEHR Embedded app: Demonstrate the ability to perform an EHR launch to a SMART on FHIR\n\n•\n\nSmart Backend Services App (Multi-patient authorization and API) : These are server-to-server backend applications e.g. Export\nclinical data for multiple patients in a group. This app is system level app without any UI.\n\nTypes of Authentications supported\n•\n\nSymmetric (“client secret”) authentication\n\n•\n\nAsymmetric (“private key JWT”) authentication\n\n•\n\nPublic Clients","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01KJqee2XdC5XskkXRhYdV7g","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01QUYtStY9Bo9wXjyvmkRdLX","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/strateq-health-inc--strateqehr/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Strateq Health, Inc. — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-16\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://strateqhealth.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Strateq-Export.pdf\n- CHPL ID: 10778 (15.05.05.3097.STRQ.01.00.1.220105)\n- Mandatory Disclosures: https://strateqhealth.com/resources/product-certification/\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe**: HTTP HEAD request to the registered URL returned `200 OK`, `Content-Type: application/pdf`, `Content-Length: 282110` bytes. The URL is a direct PDF download — no redirects, no login, no JavaScript required.\n\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://strateqhealth.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Strateq-Export.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n```\n\n2. **Downloaded the PDF**:\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://strateqhealth.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Strateq-Export.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o downloads/Strateq-Export.pdf\n```\n\n3. **Verified the file**: `file` confirms it is a PDF document. `pdfinfo` reports 1 page, A4, created 2023-12-06 from \"Microsoft Word - Export.docx\" via \"Microsoft: Print To PDF\". No embedded files, no embedded URLs.\n\n4. **Checked the certification/mandatory disclosures page** at `https://strateqhealth.com/resources/product-certification/` for additional EHI export documentation. The page lists certification criteria and has a section \"API and EHI EXPORT\" that reads: \"In accordance with 170.315(b)(10) EHR certification criteria, please click below for our full EHI Export documentation.\" The link points to the same `Strateq-Export.pdf` already downloaded. No additional export-related documents were found.\n\n5. **Checked other files on the certification page**: The page links to several other PDFs (Real-World Testing plans/results for 2023–2025 and a Smart on FHIR API document). The API document (`Strateq-SmartOnFHIR-API.pdf`, 66 pages, updated 2026-02-10) covers the (g)(10) FHIR API — it documents standard US Core FHIR resources via SMART on FHIR and is not related to the (b)(10) EHI export mechanism.\n\n6. **Checked ValidURLs.json**: The FHIR endpoint listing (`https://testauth.strateqhealth.com/SmartOnFHIR/ValidURLs.json`) contains FHIR Endpoint and Organization resources for the SMART on FHIR API. Not related to EHI export.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of **a single A4 page with 6 sentences**. Here is the full text:\n\n> **Product Name and Version: StrateqEHR, Version 5**\n>\n> The patient EHI export contains data from the patient's chart. Multiple file formats are used to store this information.\n>\n> ZIP is an archive file format.\n>\n> PDF or Portable Document Format is a file format that is used to present text or image based documents.\n>\n> C-CDA or Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture is a file format used for health information exchange.\n>\n> The export file itself is a zip file. It contains zip files of C-CDAs and other files attached to the patient's chart (e.g. PDF and images)\n>\n> Information for each patient encounter is available C-CDA format in zip archive.\n\nThat's it. The document describes the export as a ZIP file containing:\n- C-CDA documents (one per patient encounter), themselves in ZIP archives\n- Other files attached to the patient's chart (PDFs, images)\n\nThere is no data dictionary, no field definitions, no schema documentation, no sample data, no export instructions, no screenshots, and no information about how to initiate the export or what specific data elements are included.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nBased on the product research, StrateqEHR is a comprehensive hospital information system storing:\n- Patient demographics and registration data\n- Clinical documentation (H&P, assessments, care plans, nursing notes, dictation notes, operative notes)\n- Orders (medications, labs, radiology, nursing, procedures via CPOE)\n- Medication data (prescriptions, medication lists, home medications, medication reconciliation, eMAR)\n- Lab results (via Aspyra CyberLAB integration)\n- Vital signs and clinical observations\n- ED tracking data\n- Scanned documents and images\n- Medical record deficiency tracking\n- Billing and claims data (charges, claims, remittance, eligibility, denials, GL journal entries)\n- Scheduling data\n- C-CDA documents\n- Immunization records\n- Clinical quality measure data\n- Implantable device data\n\nThe export documentation says the export contains \"data from the patient's chart\" in C-CDA format plus attached files (PDFs, images). This is deeply inadequate for the following reasons:\n\n**C-CDA covers only a subset of clinical data.** C-CDA (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture) is standardized for clinical summaries — it handles problems, medications, allergies, labs, vitals, immunizations, procedures, and clinical notes reasonably well. However, it does not naturally represent:\n\n- **Billing and revenue cycle data**: Charges, claims, remittance, eligibility, denial management, GL journal entries, patient account balances. This is a major gap — StrateqEHR has an extensive revenue cycle module with Waystar integration. None of this data fits in C-CDA.\n- **Order details**: While C-CDA can capture medication orders and some procedure orders, the close-loop CPOE data (lab orders, radiology orders, nursing orders, complaint-specific order sets) with their full lifecycle would not be preserved in a C-CDA clinical summary.\n- **eMAR administration records**: Medication administration records with timestamps, administering nurse, held/refused status, etc. are richer than what a C-CDA medication section typically carries.\n- **ED tracking data**: ESI levels, arrival times, dispositions, length of stay, turnaround times — operational ED data that doesn't map to C-CDA sections.\n- **Dynamic Form Engine content**: StrateqEHR's patent-pending Dynamic Form Engine renders custom clinical forms. Whether the full structured data from these forms survives C-CDA serialization is unknown and undocumented.\n- **Perioperative data**: Operative checklists, resource scheduling, perioperative documentation — the level of detail preserved in C-CDA is unclear.\n- **HIM data**: Document scanning metadata, deficiency tracking, release of information records.\n- **Implantable device data**: While C-CDA can carry UDI information, the documentation doesn't confirm this is included.\n\n**The documentation provides no specifics.** We cannot determine:\n- Which C-CDA document types are generated (CCD, Discharge Summary, Progress Note, etc.)\n- Which C-CDA sections are populated\n- Whether custom or non-standard data is exported at all\n- Whether billing data is included in any form\n- What \"other files attached to the patient's chart\" encompasses beyond PDFs and images\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Format**: ZIP archive containing per-encounter C-CDA documents (also zipped) and attached files (PDF, images)\n- **Standard**: C-CDA is a recognized HL7 standard (good), but it's designed for clinical summaries and transitions of care, not comprehensive EHI export\n- **Appropriateness**: C-CDA is a reasonable format for clinical data but is fundamentally a summary format. Using it as the sole export mechanism for a full HIS that includes revenue cycle, ED operations, and custom form data means significant data domains are likely excluded or lossy. A proper (b)(10) export for this product would need supplementary formats (CSV, database dump, etc.) for the data that doesn't fit in C-CDA.\n- **Reconstructability**: Without a data dictionary or field mapping, a third party cannot determine what data is present or missing in the export. They would need to parse the C-CDAs and hope the standard sections cover what they need.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThis is among the weakest EHI export documentation possible while still technically existing. Specific failures:\n\n- **No data dictionary**: No listing of tables, fields, data types, or value sets\n- **No field-level definitions**: No information about what specific data elements are exported\n- **No export instructions**: No information about how a user initiates the export, what parameters are available, or what the workflow looks like\n- **No sample data**: No example C-CDA documents, no sample export files\n- **No schema documentation**: No reference to which C-CDA templates or sections are used\n- **No format specification**: Beyond naming C-CDA, ZIP, and PDF, no details about file naming conventions, directory structure within the ZIP, encoding, or version information\n- **Definitional padding**: Three of the six sentences are generic definitions of file formats (what ZIP is, what PDF is, what C-CDA is) that add no value\n- **A developer could not implement an import** based on this documentation. They would know to expect a ZIP with C-CDAs inside, but nothing about the content, structure, or completeness of those C-CDAs.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: None. There are no tables, no fields, no data types, no descriptions, no cardinality information.\n- **Coded fields**: Not documented\n- **Relationships**: Not documented\n- **Versioning**: The PDF was created 2023-12-06 and has not been updated since. The filename and creation metadata suggest it was a quick Word document printed to PDF.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://strateqhealth.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Strateq-Export.pdf\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none (Cloudflare present but no challenge served)\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\nNone — the PDF was immediately accessible. The obstacle is the content, not the access. The entire EHI export documentation for a comprehensive hospital information system is 6 sentences on a single page, three of which are definitions of common file formats.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":477,"cache_read_input_tokens":47453,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":477},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"80fc4201-dcd6-4264-b166-6d2ac80f9aca","uuid":"445ca912-bb23-4dfd-8f6c-156de70fb9a0"}
